answer: Each challenge derives a domain-separated instance from its task data and a future drand threshold-BLS beacon pulse. Because the pulse remains unpredictable until quorum signatures arrive and is publicly verifiable, an attacker cannot precompute valid answers, rank identities, or farm responses offline. Revealed randomness binds eligibility and scoring to that round, so copper, onyx, and ridge swarms gain no advantage by spawning sybils.
